evidence: FIFA's own site (inside.fifa.com, disciplinary update dated 2026-07-29) states the Disciplinary Committee OPENED proceedings against Molina, Paredes, Ayala, Almada and Gavi and that the respondents have now been given the opportunity to present their position, following which a decision will be issued in due course. ESPN and Al Jazeera 2026-07-29 report the same: charges opened, no sanction imposed. No FIFA decision imposing a suspension or fine dated on or before 2026-08-10 was found.
disconfirming: FIFA did act inside the window - formal charges on 2026-07-29, including three assault counts against Paredes - so a reading on the spirit rather than the text would score this a hit. beIN and Yahoo on 2026-07-30 both describe sanctions as still pending with no announced timetable.
note: The criterion demands a disciplinary ACTION such as suspension or fine; FIFA opened proceedings and expressly deferred the decision. Charges are not sanctions. The distinction is the whole verdict.

evidence: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree announced a maritime embargo effective immediately on 2026-07-20, and deputy media office head Nasruddin Amer stated Bab el-Mandeb would be closed (Euronews, 2026-07-20). Al Jazeera 2026-07-20 headlines the declaration. NPR 2026-07-21 reports the Houthis have announced a naval blockade of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and that commercial vessels have begun rerouting per ship trackers. Northeastern 2026-07-21 reports the same.
disconfirming: The blockade was framed as an embargo against Saudi Arabia rather than a closure of the strait as such; NBC 2026-08-03 describes it as a declaration they WOULD impose a complete blockade with no specifics given. Fox cites US and regional experts saying the Houthis lack capability to fully shut the strait. One commentary notes the strait is not physically blockaded, only commercially dead.
note: ALREADY-DECIDED RISK: the Houthi declaration is dated 2026-07-20, one day BEFORE this row was issued on 2026-07-21. If the packet carried it, the outcome existed at seal. That matters more than the verdict.

evidence: AP reporting carried by NPR 2026-07-28 states the crisis prompted the government to declare a national emergency for wildfires for the first time; PBS NewsHour carries the same AP line, the government declared a national emergency over the fires. Timing falls inside the 2026-07-27 to 2026-08-10 window.
disconfirming: Both reports I could verify trace to a single wire service (AP), so the criterion's two independent wire services test is not independently satisfied by what I found. Al Jazeera 2026-07-27 records a national emergency declaration for SPAIN on 2026-07-24 and quotes the French PM only on X, which is a live confusion risk between the two countries.
note: Two separate gaps: a national emergency declared by the national government is not obviously a NATIONWIDE state of emergency in the French legal sense, and I could confirm only one wire service where the criterion demands two. The underlying event is well attested; the criterion's specific terms are not. An adjudicator leaning HIT has real grounds and should say which reading he used.

evidence: ABC News 2026-07-28 reports Zelenskyy and Netanyahu met separately with Trump in the Oval Office that Tuesday, with White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt posting that Trump had concluded his meetings with both. Fortune 2026-07-28 reports Netanyahu calling the White House visit excellent and notes Zelenskyy met Trump earlier the same day. Photographs are captioned Oval Office, Washington, July 28, 2026.
disconfirming: None found. The meetings were separate rather than joint, but the criterion requires both leaders in a face-to-face meeting with Trump, not a single joint meeting.
note: Both meetings occurred on US soil on 2026-07-28, inside the window, and were confirmed by a White House spokesperson posting plus multiple outlets. This is the cleanest of the four.
